s: Verb suffix for the second-person singular.
lachen (“to laugh”) + -st → du lachst (“you laugh, thou laughest”)
spielen (“to play”) + -st → du spielst (“you play, thou playest”)
-st.et: From Middle High German -est, from older -es through rebracketing in inverted forms like sizzes du → sizzestu → sizzest du (“do you sit”). Further from a merger of various Old High German conjugation suffixes, from Proto-Germanic, from Proto-Indo-European.

s: Forms superlatives of adjectives and adverbs, sometimes triggering umlaut.
-st.et: From Middle High German -est, from a merger of Old High German -ist and -ōst, from Proto-Germanic *-istaz and *-ōstaz.
